testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to start working after you press the brake pedal
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to start working after you press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the air lines to the brakes. Because of this, there is always a delay between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes actually start working. This delay is usually at least half a second.

questions.question: The air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold enough air for only one brake use.
Hold enough air for several brake uses even if the compressor stops working.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several brake uses even if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air so you can still brake several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor starts and stops pumping air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Which of the following is not part of a vehicle's air brake system?
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, governor, storage tanks, tank drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, pressure gauges, warning signals, stop light switch, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment will wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check your brake adjustment often to avoid brake problems.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum
Press against the inside of the brake drum

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum
questions.explanation: Friction happens inside the brake drum when the brake shoes and linings push against the drum's inside surface. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Using the brakes creates heat. If too much heat builds up:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual
The brakes will not work evenly

questions.explanation: Brakes are built to handle a lot of heat. However, do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. If brakes get too hot, they can fade and lose power. Use engine braking to help slow your vehicle.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. If one system has an air leak, the other system may still work normally.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning comes on, you should:

options.text: Keep driving, but get the brakes fixed within a week
Pull over and check the brakes
Call a mechanic while you are driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning comes on, stop your vehicle safely while you still have brake control. Check and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has two separate brake systems that use one set of controls
Is one brake system with two different sets of controls
Has one system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate brake systems that use one set of controls
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. Usually one system controls the rear brakes and the other controls the front brakes.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during an applied leakage test. This is the safe limit for your vehicle.

questions.question: How long should it take air pressure to build up in a single air system?
questions.explanation: In a single air system, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi within three minutes.

questions.question: What color lights show that anti-lock brakes are not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights that turn on when there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Prevent your vehicle from accelerating when going uphill.

questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) prevent your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: During an inspection, how much should slack adjusters on S-cam brakes move?
questions.explanation: Check slack adjusters on level ground with the parking brake released. Pull each slack adjuster. It should not move more than about one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it may be out of adjustment and needs to be fixed.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi. Vehicles with air brakes must have a low pressure warning device.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that spring brakes turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, chock the wheels and step on and off the brake pedal to release air from the system. The parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should turn on.

questions.question: What happens if ABS is on only one axle?

options.text: Still allows you additional control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still allows you additional control when braking.
questions.explanation: If ABS is on only the tractor, only the trailer, or only one axle, you will still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: What do the two systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor is damaged, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should be no more than 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven and needs repairs.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure in an air brake tank drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must turn on before pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning does not work during inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: What can happen if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Using the brake pedal too often lets air out of the system faster than the compressor can replace it. Air brakes may fail if pressure drops too low.

questions.question: On flat surfaces, wheel chocks:

options.text: Can stop a parked vehicle from moving.
Make it easier for a parked vehicle to roll.
Should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can stop a parked vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When a parking brake cannot be used, wheel chocks hold a parked vehicle in place on a level surface.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only if you have used the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks when parking on level ground. This is essential if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This helps a driver know if brakes are starting to fade.
